metadata.description: Curated crop disease reference used to ground AI visual observations. Treatment guidance is general and avoids product-specific dosage instructions.

symptoms: Dark brown concentric rings or target-like spots on older leaves
Yellowing around leaf spots
Spots may spread to stems and fruit
Lower leaves are usually affected first
possible_causes: Warm, humid conditions and extended leaf wetness
Poor air circulation and overhead irrigation
Infected crop debris remaining in the field
prevention: Use healthy seed and disease-free transplants
Rotate with non-solanaceous crops
Remove and destroy severely infected plant debris
Water at the base and avoid prolonged leaf wetness
Maintain spacing for better airflow
treatment_guidance: Remove badly infected lower leaves and dispose of them away from the field
Consult your local KVK or extension officer for a locally registered fungicide and follow the product label exactly
Avoid spraying during windy conditions or close to harvest; observe the label waiting period
diseases.reference_source: ICAR and state agricultural university extension guidance on Alternaria leaf blight

symptoms: Large irregular water-soaked grey-green patches on leaves
White fuzzy growth on the underside of leaves in humid weather
Brown lesions on stems
Fruit develops firm brown patches
possible_causes: Cool, wet weather with high humidity
Spread by wind-driven rain and infected plant material
prevention: Use certified disease-free planting material
Avoid dense planting and improve field ventilation
Remove infected plants immediately
Do not compost infected plant material
treatment_guidance: Act quickly because late blight can spread rapidly
Remove and destroy infected plants
Contact the local agriculture department or KVK for a recommended locally approved control programme
Follow local resistance-management guidance and product labels
diseases.reference_source: ICAR and state agricultural university extension guidance on Phytophthora blight

symptoms: Water-soaked dark lesions on leaves
White fungal-like growth on leaf undersides in wet conditions
Rapid collapse of foliage
Brown rot on tubers
possible_causes: Cool, humid weather and prolonged leaf wetness
Infected seed tubers and volunteer plants
prevention: Plant certified seed potatoes
Avoid overhead irrigation late in the day
Destroy cull piles and volunteer plants
Maintain adequate spacing for airflow
treatment_guidance: Remove infected foliage and isolate affected areas
Seek immediate guidance from the local agriculture office or KVK because the disease spreads quickly
Use only locally registered products and follow label directions
diseases.reference_source: ICAR and state agricultural university extension guidance on potato late blight

symptoms: Yellow to orange powdery pustules in stripes on leaves
Pustules arranged in rows along leaf veins
Yellowing and premature drying of leaves
Severe infection reduces grain filling
possible_causes: Cool temperatures with moisture and dew
Wind-borne spores and susceptible wheat varieties
prevention: Grow recommended rust-resistant wheat varieties
Avoid excessive nitrogen application
Sow at the recommended time for your district
Monitor crops closely during cool, humid weather
treatment_guidance: Report unusual rust outbreaks to the local agriculture department
Consult the district agriculture officer or KVK for the current recommended fungicide schedule
Follow product labels and local resistance-management advice

symptoms: Spindle-shaped or diamond-shaped lesions on leaves
Grey centres with brown margins
Lesions may join and kill leaf tissue
Neck blast can cause panicle breakage
possible_causes: High humidity, dew and moderately warm temperatures
Excess nitrogen and dense crop canopy
prevention: Use recommended resistant varieties where available
Apply nitrogen in split doses as per soil test
Maintain balanced plant nutrition
Avoid continuous standing water where not recommended
treatment_guidance: Consult the local agriculture office or KVK for a district-specific management plan
Use only registered fungicides and follow the label and waiting period
Keep a field record of symptoms and weather conditions
diseases.reference_source: ICAR and state rice research station advisory

symptoms: Upward or downward curling of leaves
Thickened, darkened veins
Small leaf-like enations on leaf undersides
Stunted growth and reduced boll formation
prevention: Use recommended virus-resistant or tolerant varieties
Monitor and manage whitefly populations as per local guidance
Remove infected volunteer plants
Avoid late sowing where whitefly pressure is high
treatment_guidance: There is no direct cure for the virus; focus on vector management and removing severely infected plants
Contact the local KVK for integrated whitefly management guidance
Use only approved insecticides when thresholds require it and follow label instructions

symptoms: Ragged holes in leaves
Moist sawdust-like frass in the whorl
Larvae with an inverted Y on the head
Damage concentrated in the growing point
possible_causes: Fall armyworm larvae feeding on leaves and whorls
Continuous maize cultivation and warm weather
prevention: Scout fields regularly, especially the whorl
Encourage natural enemies and follow integrated pest management
Avoid staggered maize planting that provides continuous food
Follow district pest surveillance alerts
treatment_guidance: Hand-pick larvae where practical in small plots
Consult the local KVK for threshold-based integrated pest management
If a registered insecticide is advised, follow the label rate, safety precautions and waiting period
diseases.reference_source: ICAR and state maize pest surveillance advisory

symptoms: Sunken circular lesions on fruit
Dark spots with concentric rings on fruit and leaves
Fruit rot and premature fruit drop
Lesions may develop during humid weather
possible_causes: High humidity and rain during fruiting
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed
Rotate crops and remove infected debris
Avoid overhead irrigation during fruiting
Provide good drainage and plant spacing
treatment_guidance: Remove infected fruit from the field
Consult the local KVK or extension officer for an approved fungicide schedule
Follow the product label and pre-harvest interval
diseases.reference_source: ICAR and state horticulture extension guidance

symptoms: Small white sunken spots that enlarge into purple lesions
Brown-purple patches on leaves and seed stalks
Leaf tips dry and die back
Severe infection reduces bulb size
possible_causes: Prolonged leaf wetness and humid weather
prevention: Use healthy sets or seed
Rotate with non-allium crops
Avoid overhead irrigation and improve airflow
Remove crop debris after harvest
treatment_guidance: Remove badly affected leaves and maintain field sanitation
Consult the local horticulture office or KVK for registered control options
Follow product label directions and the waiting period
diseases.reference_source: ICAR and state horticulture extension guidance

symptoms: Yellowing and drying of upper leaves
Reddish discolouration inside split cane
Alcoholic or sour smell from affected cane
Hollow, discoloured internodes
prevention: Use disease-free seed cane from a certified source
Follow crop rotation and remove infected stools
Improve drainage in fields
Avoid planting susceptible varieties repeatedly
treatment_guidance: Uproot and destroy severely infected clumps
Avoid using seed cane from affected fields
Consult the local sugarcane research station or KVK for variety and management advice
